documents.title: RPR 6 months
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: RPR 1:8, down from 1:64 at diagnosis in October. That is better than a fourfold fall; appropriate response to treatment. Repeat at 12 months with her physical.

documents.title: Your syphilis follow-up test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Leah, good news. Your RPR has come down from 1:64 to 1:8, which is exactly the drop we want after treatment. One more check in the fall when you come in for your physical.

documents.title: RE: Your syphilis follow-up test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Oh thank god. OK see you in the fall.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

26 now, third year of grad school. Feels well. No rash, sores or discharge. Partners: still more than one; condoms 'more than before.'

No meds. NKDA. Never smoker. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a week.

Exam: vitals as charted. Skin clear, no residual rash on palms or soles. No adenopathy. Heart, lungs, abdomen normal.

A/P
1. Early syphilis, treated 10/2021: 12-month RPR drawn today.
2. High-risk sexual behavior: reviewed condoms and testing every 3-6 months while she has multiple partners.
3. Pap done 2021; next 2024.
4. Flu and bivalent COVID booster today, opposite arms.

Physical next October.

documents.title: RPR 12 months
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: RPR 1:2. Sustained decline from 1:64; serologic response adequate. Early syphilis marked resolved. A low titer may persist. Patient notified through portal.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 7 days

documents.title: Gynecology Office Visit (outside)
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN OFFICE NOTE
Date of service: 11/01/2022
Faxed per request 1/2023

CC: burning with urination, discharge.

26 y/o G0 with a history of an ED evaluation for genital sores and our prior visits. Three days of dysuria, going more often, and a yellow vaginal discharge. Denies fever, flank or back pain, abdominal pain. LMP 2 weeks ago, normal. Multiple partners; condoms used inconsistently.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Vitals within normal limits.
Pelvic: mucopurulent discharge from the cervical os; cervical motion tenderness present.

Urine hCG negative. UA: no bacteria, no WBCs.
CT/GC NAAT: chlamydia DETECTED; gonorrhea not detected (resulted 11/3, patient informed by phone).

A/P: Chlamydia trachomatis cervicitis.
- Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 7 days, started at visit.
- Abstain 7 days after completing treatment and until partners treated; expedited partner therapy offered.
- Retest in 3 months.

documents.title: Outside prescription fill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Medication history refresh shows doxycycline hyclate 100 mg caps, #14, filled 11/1/22, prescriber at an outside OB/GYN office. No note from that office on file for this. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: FYI
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just so you know, I saw my gyn on Tuesday because it was burning when I peed and I had some discharge. They called yesterday and it was chlamydia. I'm on doxycycline twice a day for a week. Ugh. Do I need to do anything on your end?

documents.title: RE: FYI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update, Leah. Doxycycline for a week is the right treatment. Take it with a full glass of water and stay upright for a while after, and go easy on direct sun. No sex until a week after you finish and your partners have been treated. We should retest in about 3 months; I'll have the staff set that up for early February. I'll also ask your gyn's office for the visit note.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Nothing received yet from the outside OB/GYN office for the 11/1/22 visit. Called their records line, re-sent the release by fax. They said 2-3 weeks.

documents.title: Retest swab
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for 3-month test of reinfection after chlamydia treated in November. Finished all 7 days of doxycycline. No symptoms. Self-collected vaginal swab for CT/GC NAAT, instructions given. Results to portal.

documents.title: Retest negative
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Leah, your repeat swab was negative for both chlamydia and gonorrhea. You are all clear from the November infection. Keep the condoms going.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 10 days

documents.title: Outside prescription fill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fill history (weekend) shows valacyclovir 1 g tabs #20, filled Saturday 4/29/23, written by an emergency department prescriber. No ED record received. Added to med list as an outside short course; routed to PCP.

documents.title: Patient call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Went to the ED Saturday with painful blisters 'down there', burning with urination, fever and feeling run down; started about a week after sex with someone new. ED told her it looked like herpes, swabbed it, and started valacyclovir. She got a call Sunday that the swab was positive for herpes. Still sore, urinating is painful but she is managing; using sitz baths. Fever gone since yesterday. Able to urinate. Wants to be seen. Booked with PCP Thursday 5/4. Told to call back if she cannot pass urine, gets a headache with stiff neck, or the pain gets worse.

conditions.label: Primary genital herpes simplex virus infection

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
FOLLOW-UP, GENITAL HERPES

No ED record yet; history from Leah and the fill history.

About a week after unprotected sex with a new partner she developed fever and malaise, then three days of painful urination and blisters on the labia. Seen in the ED Saturday 4/29. She says they examined her, noted swollen glands in both groins, checked her urine, swabbed a sore, and started valacyclovir 1 g twice a day for 10 days. The ED called her Sunday: swab positive for herpes simplex. She does not know the type. Day 6 of valacyclovir, taking it on schedule. Fever gone. Urination still stings but is better.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Labia with several shallow healing ulcers, no new vesicles. Tender, mobile inguinal nodes on both sides. No vaginal discharge on inspection.

A/P
1. Primary genital HSV infection, healing on valacyclovir. Finish the 10 days. Sitz baths; urinating in a warm bath helps the stinging. Talked through what recurrences look like and that they tend to be milder. Disclosure to partners, condoms, no sex during sores.
2. High-risk sexual behavior: repeat STI here at any time she wants testing.
3. Requesting ED record.

documents.title: ED records follow-up
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Second request to the regional ED medical records office for the 4/29/23 visit (first sent 5/4). Voicemail left; release re-faxed. Will close the request if nothing comes.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

27, still in her graduate program. Feels well. No herpes outbreaks since the spring episode healed. No discharge, no urinary symptoms. Still dating, more than one partner at times.

The ED never sent the April record despite two requests; closed. Our chart has her account and our exam from 5/4.

No meds. NKDA. Never smoker. Alcohol unchanged.

Exam: vitals as charted. Skin clear. No lymphadenopathy. Heart, lungs, abdomen normal. Genital exam deferred, no complaints.

A/P
1. Primary genital HSV, no recurrence.
2. High-risk sexual behavior, history of syphilis and chlamydia: condoms; testing any time.
3. Pap due next year.
4. Flu and updated COVID vaccine today. Basic chemistry panel sent.

See her next fall.
